﴿And it hearkens﴾ means it heard and obeyed, concerning the splitting asunder, ﴿to its Lord, and it is right to do so﴾, meaning it is right for it to hear and obey.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 84, verse 3:

﴿And when the earth is stretched out﴾ It is increased in its extent, as a hide (adim) is stretched, and no building or mountain remains upon it.
﴿And it casts out what is within it﴾ of the dead onto its surface, ﴿and empties itself﴾ of them.

"And it hearkens to its Lord and is duly obligated" — (﴿وأَذِنَتْ﴾) it listened and obeyed in that matter, ﴿to its Lord, and it is worthy [to do so]﴾ (﴿وحُقَّتْ﴾), and all of this will happen on the Day of Resurrection. The response (jawab) of "when" (idha) and of what is conjoined to it is omitted, indicated by what follows it, its estimated meaning being: "man will meet his deeds."

O man, you are toiling toward your Lord with toil (kadhḥ), striving (jāhid) in your deeds, until (ilā) meeting (liqā’) your Lord, which is death (al-mawt), a toil (kadḥan), so you will meet it (fa-mulāqīhi), meaning you will meet your aforementioned deed, whether good or evil, on the Day of Resurrection (al-qiyāma).
﴿Then as for he who is given his record﴾ (kitab 'amalih, the book of his deeds) ﴿in his right hand﴾, he is the believer.

Surely he will be brought to a light reckoning (﴿فَسَوْفَ يُحاسَب حِسابًا يَسِيرًا﴾). That is, his deeds will be presented to him, as in the hadith in the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), in which it is said: "Whoever is subjected to close scrutiny in the reckoning will be destroyed." After the presentation, he will be pardoned for them.
ﷻ﴿And he will return to his people﴾ in the Garden, ﴿joyful﴾ at that.
﴿But as for him who is given his record behind his back﴾: he is the disbeliever, whose right hand is chained to his neck and whose left hand is placed behind his back, so he takes his record with it.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 84, verse 11:

﴿So he will call for destruction﴾ upon seeing what is in it (his record); ﴿destruction﴾, he will cry out for his own ruin, saying: "Woe to me! Destruction!" (Yā thubūrāh).

Qur'anic quotations: ﴿ويَصْلى سَعِيرًا﴾ — "and he will burn in a blazing Fire."

Translation:

﴿And he will burn in a blazing Fire﴾ — he will enter the intensely hot Fire. And in one reading (qira'ah), it is recited with a ḍammah on the yā' and a fatḥah on the ṣād, and the lām is shaddah (doubled): yuṣallā (he will be made to burn).

Translation of the passage:

"﴿Indeed, he used to be among his people﴾ his clan in the worldly life ﴿joyful﴾ exultant, insolent, through following his desires."
﴿Indeed, he thought﴾ — "an" here is the lightened form of the heavy "anna", and its noun is omitted; the meaning is that he ﴿would never return﴾ (yahur), i.e., would never go back to his Lord.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 84, verse 15:

﴿Yes [indeed]﴾, he will return to Him, ﴿surely His Lord was ever Seer of him﴾, knowing of his returning to Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 84, verse 16:

﴿So I swear not﴾ — the "lā" is extra (zā'idah); ﴿by the twilight﴾ — it is the redness in the horizon after the sun has set.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 84, verse 17:

﴿By the night and what it gathers together﴾ it gathers together whatever enters into it of creatures, such as beasts and others.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 84, verse 18:

﴿And by the moon when it becomes full﴾ — it gathers together and its light is complete, and this is on the bright nights.

﴿You will surely go﴾ O people. Its original form is تَرْكَبُونَنَّ (tarkabūnanna). The nūn of rafʿ (the nūn that marks the verb's nominative form) was deleted because of the succession of similar letters, and the wāw was deleted because two sākin letters (unvowelled letters) came together. ﴿from state to state﴾ meaning one condition after another. This refers to death, then life, and what follows them of the conditions of the Resurrection.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn, commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti, on Surah 84, verse 20:

﴿Then what is wrong with them﴾, i.e., the disbelievers, ﴿that they do not believe﴾, i.e., what prevents them from faith, or what proof they have for abandoning it, given that its proofs exist.
﴿And﴾ what is [wrong] with them that when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate﴾? (They do not) humble themselves (yakhda'un) by believing in it, because of its inimitability (i'jaz).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 84, verse 22:

﴿Nay, those who disbelieve deny﴾ the Resurrection and other things.
﴿And Allah knows best what they harbour﴾ — they gather in their records of disbelief, denial and evil deeds.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 84, verse 24:

﴿So give them good tidings﴾ inform them ﴿of a painful punishment﴾ that causes pain.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 84, verse 25:

﴿Illā﴾ (but) ﴿those who believe and do righteous deeds, theirs is a reward never to be cut off﴾ — not cut off, nor diminished, nor is it reckoned as a favour upon them.
